hints: A valid course order exists only if the dependency graph has no directed cycle.
Compute each course's indegree, the number of prerequisites still unmet.
Repeatedly output any zero-indegree course and reduce indegrees of its outgoing neighbors.
analogy: Take any course whose prerequisites are all cleared, then unlock courses that depend on it.
example: For 1->3 and 2->3, either 1,2,3 or 2,1,3 is valid.
algorithm: Use Kahn's algorithm with a queue of indegree-zero vertices. If fewer than n are output, a cycle remains and no order exists.
correctness: Every output vertex has no incoming edge from an unprocessed vertex, so prerequisites precede dependents; failure to output all vertices means the remainder has no zero-indegree node and contains a cycle.
